label: Telegram notification connector
summary: Prepare redacted Telegram Bot API event delivery to explicitly enrolled chats and recipients.
core_boundary: Telegram messages and chat membership do not grant Core login, command execution or incident-response authority. Essential local email and alerts remain free Core capabilities. This is a design-only connector proposal. Essential hosting, current actor and tenant authorization, native service drivers and recovery remain in the free Core. No production interface, publisher trust, installation or effectful capability is established by this metadata.
acceptance: Qualify bot credentials, recipient/chat ownership, explicit enrollment and per-tenant disclosure rules; do not accept browser-supplied arbitrary destinations.
Begin with outbound notifications; any optional incoming webhook requires secret-token validation, replay/idempotency controls and separate current Core actor authorization.
Bound message size, retry, rate and retention; distinguish provider acceptance from delivery evidence and preserve local alerts when tokens or destinations are revoked.

Declare observation-only, import or externally managed ownership before any integration request. Refuse competing writers for Core-owned resources; ownership handoff requires an authorized inventory, admission review and recovery plan.

Before implementation, qualify an explicitly selected provider/interface revision, supported compatibility matrix, immutable package provenance, dependency inventory and licensing model; no release is admitted by this proposal.

Enforce current Core actor, tenant and capability checks at each admitted request; keep credentials in scoped secret references, redact diagnostics and reject arbitrary destinations, shell commands or host/container sockets.

Demonstrate that disablement, removal, provider outage and commercial entitlement loss preserve essential Core access, hosted workloads, local audit and recovery; retain owned data unless a separately authorized purge is requested.
